sentences.text: Thalassomedon is a genus of plesiosaur named by Welles in 1943, derived from Greek words meaning "sea lord".
It ranks among the largest elasmosaurids, with estimated lengths between 10.86 and 11.95 meters and masses ranging from 4.4 to 6.8 metric tons.
This creature possessed a very long neck comprising 62 vertebrae, measuring about 5.9 meters, and a skull 47 centimeters long containing teeth that were 5 centimeters long.
The flippers of Thalassomedon measured between 1.5 and 2 meters in length.
Over half the animal's total body length was dedicated to a neck spanning 62 vertebrae.
Stones recovered from the stomach region sparked theories that they served as ballast or aided digestion.
Six specimens of Thalassomedon in varying states of preservation are currently displayed in museums across the United States.
Thalassomedon belongs to the family Elasmosauridae and its closest relative is Elasmosaurus.
This genus of plesiosaur appeared in North America about 95 million years ago.
The time range for Thalassomedon is the Cenomanian, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
